title: CRLR/119/2018 of Smt. Pushpa Badoni Vs Smt. Anita Badoni AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 119 of 2018
Smt. Pushpa Badoni Ö..Revisionist
Versus
Smt. Anita Badoni & others Ö.Respondents
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. S.S. Adhikari, A.G.A. along with Mr. P.S. Uniyal, Brief Holder for the State
of Uttarakhand.
Dated: May 7, 2018
Honíble V.K. Bist, J.

This Criminal Revision has been filed by the
revisionist to set-aside the judgment and order dated
30.1.2018 passed by the 1st Additional Sessions Judge,
Rishikesh, Dehradun in Criminal Appeal No.144 of
2016, whereby the appeal filed by the revisionist against
the order dated 14.9.2016 passed by the learned
Judicial Magistrate, Rishikesh Dehradun in Misc. Case
No.726 of 2015 has been dismissed.
2. Brief put, the case of the revisionist is that
the revisionist filed a Misc. Case No.726 of 2015 in the
Court of learned A.C.J.M. Rishikesh, Dehradun under
the provisions of Section 12 of the Protection of Women
from Domestic Violence Act. In the said case, the
revisionist/applicant further filed an application for
grant of interim order in her favour to the effect that,
during the pendency of the said misc. case, the
respondents may be directed to vacate the residence of
the revisionist and shall also be directed not to enter in
the said residence of the revisionist. Learned A.C.J.M.,

2
vide his order dated 14.9.2016, held that such facts
have to be decided after leading evidence and, therefore,
such an order cannot be passed at that stage and
dismissed the said case. Feeling aggrieved against the
same, revisionist preferred a Criminal Appeal under
Section 29 of the Domestic Violence Act before the
learned District and Sessions Judge, Dehradun, which
was numbered as Criminal Appeal No.144 of 2016.
Later on, the appeal was transferred to the Court of
learned 1st Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun and
the learned Sessions Judge, vide order dated
30.01.2018, dismissed the appeal filed by the
revisionist. Hence, this Criminal Revision.
3. Learned counsel for the revisionist submitted
that revisionist is an old lady, suffering from arthritis
and heart diseases. He also submitted that the
respondent no.1 on the instructions of respondent
nos.3, 4, 5 & 6 misbehaved, abused and manhandled
the revisionist and also caused physical and mental
harassment and agony to the revisionist. He further
submitted that, because of such behaviour of
respondent no.1, the revisionist asked the respondent
nos.1 & 2 to stay separately in a tenanted
accommodation; but, they refused to vacate the house
in question.
4. It is also the submission of learned counsel
for the revisionist that respondent has filed a complaint
before the State Women Commission and, on account of
the family pressure, the revisionist entered into a
compromise with the respondent and the respondent
no.1 was granted permission to stay on the first floor of

3
the house. He further submitted that respondent no.1
has committed cruelty and caused mental and physical
harassment to the revisionist in her own house and has
made the life of the revisionist miserable. Learned
counsel for the revisionist submitted that both the
Courts below erred in law and failed to appreciate the
law laid down by the Honíble Apex Court that a house
owned by mother-in-law or father-in-law will not come
within the definition of shared household and the
respondent no.2 has no right to retain or reside over the
property in question.
5. On the other hand, learned Assistant
Government Advocate submitted that the order
impugned needs no interference of this Court and the
revision filed by the revisionist deserves to be dismissed
at the threshold.

6. I have considered the submission advanced
by the learned counsel for the parties and have perused
the impugned judgments. From the bare perusal of the
impugned judgments, it is evident that there is no
illegality in the orders passed by the Courts below. They
are correct orders. The Courts have observed that few
issues are to be decided in the case and order, as
desired, cannot be passed at this Stage. The Court has
exercised its jurisdiction in accordance with law.
7. The criminal revision is dismissed.
8. Learned counsel for the revisionist then
submitted that the matter is pending consideration
before the learned trial Court since 2015 and the

4
learned trial Court may be directed to decide the matter
at the earliest.
9. Considering the fact that the matter is
pending consideration before the learned trial Court
since 2015, the learned trial Court is directed to decide
the same very very expeditiously, without granting any
unnecessary adjournments to either of the parties. It is,
however, observed that the learned Court below shall
also bear in mind that priority should also be given to
the oldest matters.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
 07.05.2018
A.kaur
